result.title: AGORA: Reliability-Aware Aggregation of LLM Judges via Item-Response Theory
result.summary: LLM-as-a-judge is a common substitute for costly human evaluation, and aggregating several judges is the standard remedy for any single judge's bias. Judge pools mix judges of very different reliability, while the human-labeled sets that validate them hold a few hundred items or fewer. In this regime the per-item mean weights weak judges as heavily as strong ones, and confusion-table models such as Dawid-Skene must estimate a per-judge error table from too few items. We propose AGORA (Aggregation Of Reliability-weighted Assessments), an item-response-theory aggregator that places every item on one latent quality scale and describes each judge by a sensitivity parameter and ordered rating thresholds, so judge reliability is learned from all items jointly and without human labels. Across three benchmarks, AGORA matches or exceeds Dawid-Skene on large evaluation sets, and its advantage widens as the set shrinks toward a few hundred items. It remains accurate as pools grow more uneven, a label-free dispersion statistic indicates in advance when trust weighting helps, and its learned trust weights track per-judge human validity.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 AGORA，用项目反应理论把评测条目放在单一潜在质量尺度上，以敏感度参数和有序评分阈值刻画各 LLM 评审者的可靠度，在无人工标签条件下联合学习可信权重并聚合多评审打分。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「小样本标签下按可靠度加权聚合多个噪声信号」及无需标签的离散度预判指标，可能可作为 VLM 推理中多验证器或多 latent 读数融合、以及何时信任某证据线索的参考，需核查其假设是否适用于推理链评分；论文本身不涉及视觉推理。
